 November 13, 2026 at 4:30 PM EST Eric Nehm · Senior Writer, Heat Pelle Larsson's illness could make for an interesting Erik Spoelstra decision
 On the latest Miami Heat injury report, Pelle Larsson (illness) has been downgraded to doubtful, while Klay Thompson has been upgraded to probable for tonight's game against Cleveland. Larsson was inserted into the starting lineup in Sacramento on Sunday in place of Andrew Wiggins and stayed there on Tuesday in Utah.
 While Erik Spoelstra might just put Wiggins back in the starting lineup if Larsson cannot play and roll with the starting five from the team’s first nine games of the season, there’s part of me that wonders if Spoelstra tries to keep Wiggins comfortable in his role off the bench. Spoelstra was complimentary of Wiggins’ work against the Jazz in his post-practice availability on Thursday. Miami desperately needs more out of Tim Hardaway Jr. , who Spoelstra did not play in Miami’s last game.
 Could an absence from Larsson lead to a breakthrough game for Hardaway? And would Spoelstra try to use this one game to find out?
 November 13, 2026 at 4:25 PM EST Eric Koreen · Senior Editor, NBA reporting from Kaseya Center Dejounte Murray has been at the center of two regrettable trades
   Kevin C. Cox / Getty Images In June 2022, the San Antonio Spurs traded Dejounte Murray and Jock Landale to the Atlanta Hawks for Danilo Gallinari , a 2023 protected first-round pick (which turned into two second-round picks), a 2025 first-round pick (the 14th selection used on Carter Bryant ), a 2027 first-round pick and a 2026 pick swap (the Spurs exercised the swap, moving up from 29th to 20th, taking J ayden Quaintance .) The Hawks went 77-87 in Murray's two seasons in Atlanta, making the playoffs once, losing in the first round. The Hawks' top executive and head coach, who were in Atlanta when they traded for the guard, were both fired before Murray was.
 In June 2024, Atlanta traded Murray to the New Orleans Pelicans for Dyson Daniels , E.J. Lidell , Larry Nance Jr. , Cody Zeller , a 2025 first-round pick that originated from the Lakers ( Drake Powell , traded to the Nets) and a 2027 first-round pick (the less favorable of the Pelicans' and Bucks' picks, which is looking like a lottery choice, although it is protected through the top four). The Pelicans are currently 51-125 since trading for Murray. The Pelicans' top executive and head coach, who were in New Orleans when they traded for Murray, were fired before the end of Murray's second season with the team.
 Injuries certainly played a part; not all of those teams' struggles are on Murray. Many mistakes were made. Moreover, it is not as if any single player or pick given up for Murray has turned out to be a huge loss, although Bryant could be good and the pick the Hawks have this year has potential. But receiving Murray has not worked out in the least for the last two teams who traded for him.
 And yes, the Hawks will still owe the Spurs a pick for Murray, who will have been traded twice since they acquired him, so long as he is moved this season. 
 Better luck to the next team.
 November 13, 2026 at 4:15 PM EST Devon Henderson · Staff Writer, NBA Sacramento Kings guard Malik Monk partly disagreed with former NBA player Michael Beasley’s assertions that Darius Acuff should pass the ball more to get teammates involved. 
 “Mike Beasley probably don’t even watch the whole game. Probably watch the highlights, see the stats. Some of it is kind of true. But Darius been learning every game. He got better every game with giving the ball up early and getting it back, then trying to go make a play. Some games he waits to shoot in the first quarter if you watch him. So he’s learning every game. 
 So I don’t really agree with that at all.” 
 Acuff averages 7.3 assists per game on the season and 8.5 in the last four games.

 November 13, 2026 at 3:38 PM EST Devon Henderson · Staff Writer, NBA Dejounte Murray was trading barbs with fans on social media
   Megan Briggs / Getty Images In a pair of profane social media posts that have since been deleted, Dejounte Murray defended himself against fans criticizing his play and assigning him blame for the team’s recent string of blowout losses.
 Following New Orleans’ 145-111 loss to the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday, ProPelsTalk, a Pelicans podcast, posted a few clips on X highlighting Murray’s miscues. Murray responded to one in which he misplaced a pass intended for teammate Saddiq Bey, resulting in a turnover.
 “Ohhhhh let’s talk about it,” Murray wrote back on X in a since-deleted post. “When you run post plays, are they suppose to catch on the block or the 3pt line? Let’s hear it Mr social media coach, Gm and President? You have no f—ing clue what we dealing with. 
 “Maybe you should ask the whole team individually how they feel on a serious note and then … rethink alot of s—.” 
 That interaction followed a previous post he also deleted in which he responded to an account noting that the Pelicans are 1-8 this season with him on the floor and 3-0 without him.
 “From what’s going on INSIDE, this sounds like someone hit you to say this!!” Murray wrote. “THE ‘SABOTAGE’ IS REAL!!”

 November 13, 2026 at 3:30 PM EST William Guillory · Staff Writer, Rockets Murray's time in New Orleans seemed cursed from the jump
 It seemed like Dejounte Murray's time in New Orleans was destined to fail.   Rob Gray / Imagn Images Today’s news of Dejounte Murray requesting a trade out of New Orleans seems to mark the end of a Murray-Pelicans marriage that was pretty much a disaster from the start.
 Murray broke his hand during his first game. A few months later, he tore his Achilles and was sidelined for a year. When he returned, the lead executive ( David Griffin ) who traded for him and the coach ( Willie Green ) he played for in his first game were both already fired.
 Rumblings about Murray’s displeasure in New Orleans started to creep out before he even came back from the Achilles injury. He appeared on “The Pivot Podcast” in the summer of 2025 and said New Orleans wasn’t the team he thought he was getting traded to the previous summer, and that his first season with the Pels was his “worst experience playing in the NBA.”
 Murray’s place in New Orleans grew even more tenuous after the team drafted Jeremiah Fears with the No. 7 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft as the point guard of the future. It was only a matter of time before this breakup happened, but Murray’s attitude on the court and his recent tweets lashing out at the team made it clear that it was time to bring this marriage to an end.
 Now, the question is how long will the Pels make Murray wait for a trade. Are there any suitors out there willing to give anything of value to acquire the 30-year-old point guard who can potentially become an unrestricted free agent next summer?

 November 13, 2026 at 3:20 PM EST Christian Clark · Senior Writer, Mavericks reporting from Rocket Arena Dejounte Murray's tenure in New Orleans filled with injuries and toxicity 
 It looks like Dejounte Murray ’s time in New Orleans is over after only 54 games. Murray has requested a trade, our Will Guillory confirmed Friday . Murray has been mixing it up with Pelicans fans on social media this past week, some of whom have latched onto the fact that New Orleans is 1-8 with Murray in the lineup and 3-0 when he sits this season.
 The Pelicans, who acquired Murray in a 2024 trade from the Atlanta Hawks, surrendered Dyson Daniels and two first-round picks to get him. Murray broke his hand in his first game with the Pelicans and, a few months later, he tore his Achilles. The executive who traded for him, David Griffin , was fired after Murray’s first season with the Pelicans. Joe Dumars , who replaced Griffin as the team’s lead decision-maker, will now see if he can find a landing spot for the unhappy 30-year-old guard. With how toxic the situation has gotten, it’s hard to imagine Murray ever wearing a Pelicans uniform again.
 November 13, 2026 at 3:18 PM EST Sam Amick · Senior Writer, NBA Source: Dejounte Murray interested in joining Suns
   Stephen Lew / Imagn Images According to a league source with knowledge of Dejounte Murray's situation, the Pelicans' guard has strong interest in joining the Phoenix Suns. His camp has been hopeful that a deal would materialize in which he would be swapped for Suns guard Jalen Green . 
 Team sources on both sides recently insisted there had not been any talks between the teams about that deal. But that certainly could change.
 November 13, 2026 at 3:10 PM EST John Hollinger · Senior Writer, NBA reporting from Kaseya Center Why Dejounte Murray saga could drag out
   Lachlan Cunningham / Getty Images Demanding a trade when you have no trade value is definitely quite a flex, especially in mid-November when deals are exceptionally rare. Dejounte Murray just missed an entire season but makes $32.8 million this year and $30.8 million in 2027-28 on a player option for next year the he’d be extremely likely to pick up. (There are also some incentives in there that seem rather unlikely at the moment).
 As a result, about the only plausible endgame in the short term would be a buyout agreement where Murray leaves money on the table and/or surrenders his player option year so that he can sign someplace else. Otherwise, this seems likely to drag on until other teams are more ready to deal, with sometime after Dec. 15 (when many 2026 free agents become trade-eligible) a more plausible timeframe.
 If it ends in a buyout, removing Murray’s player option would not likely make the Pelicans a cap-room player in 2027 unless they shed another contract or two. But it would give them considerable financial flexibility to add players in trades and with exception money. (PS - Raise your hand if you had Jordan Poole lasting longer in New Orleans than Murray)
 Alas, the Pelicans will only have one first-round draft pick this spring, and not two, because they traded the lesser of their own pick and Milwaukee’s to Atlanta … for Dejounte Murray.
 November 13, 2026 at 3:04 PM EST The Athletic NBA Staff BREAKING: Pelicans' Dejounte Murray requests trade
 By Josh Robbins, William Guillory and Sam Amick 
 Dejounte Murray has asked the New Orleans Pelicans for a trade.
 The 30-year-old guard’s desire for a new home — first reported by ESPN and confirmed by The Athletic through a team source — comes as the Pelicans have opened their season 4-8 and sit in 12th place in the Western Conference standings.
 Per a league source with knowledge of Murray’s situation, the Pelicans guard has strong interest in joining the Phoenix Suns. Murray’s camp has been hopeful that a deal would materialize in which he would be swapped for Suns guard Jalen Green. A Suns team source told The Athletic on Friday that there have been no talks as yet about a possible Green-for-Murray deal.
 Sources spoke on the condition of anonymity given the sensitive nature of the discussions.
 Read the latest below.

 November 13, 2026 at 1:04 PM EST Mike Vorkunov · Staff Writer, NBA and Basketball Business Writer NBA’s Terry Rozier investigation could become part of illegal gambling trial
   The NBA’s investigation into veteran guard Terry Rozier for alleged sports gambling may become part of the government’s case at trial next year.
 Lawyers for the Department of Justice have asked the federal judge overseeing the case to allow evidence that Rozier lied during the course of the NBA’s investigation into whether Rozier took himself out early from a March 2023 Charlotte Hornets game as part of an illegal gambling scheme. Attorneys for Rozier asked the judge to compel the NBA to hand over the full results of that investigation if prosecutors intend to use parts of it at trial and say that the league has so far only shared outlines of it orally and not its entire report.
 The NBA’s role in the Rozier case, and what it found during its investigation three years ago, became a focal point of the federal case this week after attorneys for Rozier and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of New York traded legal filings that each asked Judge LaShann DeArcy Hall to access the NBA’s investigation as part of their case.
 Full Story November 13, 2026 at 2:44 PM EST Joe Vardon · Senior Writer, NBA No Evan Mobley for Cavs tonight
   Jason Miller / Getty Images The Cavaliers start a back-to-back tonight in Miami, and Evan Mobley is listed as OUT against the Heat with a sprained toe. 
 The play on which he was injured looked like a sprained stomach. In the fourth quarter of Cleveland’s win over the Knicks at Madison Square Garden Wednesday, Mobley got caught in the air and couldn’t land on his feet. He did a belly smack onto the hardwood, or so it appeared. His left big toe also crashed into the court on the fall (imagine a T-bone car crash), and while he stayed in the game, he was complaining about his toe immediately afterwards. 
 We will see if he is able to play Saturday in Cleveland against the Mavericks.
 November 13, 2026 at 2:30 PM EST Sam Amick · Senior Writer, NBA What's Jalen Green's future with the Suns?
   Kelsey Grant / Getty Images When Phoenix owner Mat Ishbia approved the Kevin Durant trade with Houston in the summer of 2025, it was because the Rockets had finally relented on the players that the Suns coveted. And Jalen Green , the No. 2 pick in the 2021 draft who was entering his fifth season at the time, was seen internally as a must-have part of the package.
 “(It) was never gonna get done without Jalen and Dillon (Brooks) in the deal,” Ishbia told me earlier this year. “ Those are the two players we wanted. It wasn’t, ‘Hey, how do we fill a salary with these numbers?’ It was, ‘In order to have Kevin Durant on your team, I want Dillon Brooks to help me with my culture and my identity. I want Jalen Green as a 23-year-old up-and-coming leading scorer.’” 
 They landed Green, of course, but that last part about him heading up their offensive efforts has simply not come to bear for these Suns (5-6). After averaging 21 points per game in his final Rockets season, Green’s scoring dipped to 17.8 in his first season with the Suns (in just 32 games) and currently stands at just 11.8 through his first 10 games (he’s fourth in scoring behind Devin Booker , Miles Bridges and Brooks). In turn, there is a great deal of interest around the league in how Phoenix will handle Green (who has a player option worth $36 million for next season) heading into the deadline.
 The outside belief is that they are motivated to swap Green for a proven point guard. The Suns, according to a team source, insist that they’ll remain patient with their roster and don’t plan to truly engage in trade talks, potentially, until later in the season.
